About Ixian

Ixian Robotics is building intelligent machines to reindustrialize America. We’re based in San Francisco and backed by a16z and Accel.

We believe robotics is a full-stack problem. Software, hardware, and machine learning are only part of it. Bridging advances in robot learning with America’s industrial base requires invention in how we understand customers, design products, navigate supply chains, and make the economics work. We’re building a company that takes responsibility for all of it.

At Ixian, deployment isn’t the final step after the “real innovation” is complete. Deploying robots is the point of robotics, and deployment is our forcing function for innovation. Putting a machine to work reveals what the lab can’t: what breaks, what matters to the people using it, and what it will take to make our machines indispensable.

Robots are called machines when they work. We intend to build machines.

About the role

You’ll build software that helps our engineers develop, test, and operate robotics systems. Working with the team, you’ll take on a defined project that could involve developer tools, data processing, test automation, or software that interfaces with hardware.

You’ll follow your work through implementation, testing, and use by the people it supports. We’re looking for someone who enjoys understanding a problem, building a practical solution, and improving it based on real feedback. Your project will reflect your skills and the team’s current needs.

What you’ll do

- Build a focused tool, service, or software component that solves a concrete problem for our engineering or operations team.

- Write and test code for tasks such as processing sensor data, inspecting logs, automating checks, or simplifying repeated workflows.

- Work with engineers to reproduce bugs, investigate failures, and understand how software behaves when connected to physical systems.

- Document setup steps, expected behavior, and known limitations so other people can use and maintain what you build.

- Incorporate code review and user feedback, and help verify that your changes work in the environment where they will run.

What you’ll bring

- Programming experience from coursework, research, personal projects, a robotics team, or a previous internship. Examples of working software are welcome.

- Comfort with Python or another general-purpose language, plus a basic understanding of data structures, debugging, and version control.

- A habit of checking your work and breaking unfamiliar problems into smaller steps you can test and understand.

- Curiosity about robotics and willingness to learn the hardware, data, and operational context behind a software problem.

- Clear communication and dependable follow-through. Experience with Linux, C++, sensors, or robotics software is useful but not required.

Role Overview

REGENT is reinventing coastal transportation with the Seaglider, a vehicle that flies over water on a cushion of air, and getting that vehicle's performance right — both on the drawing board and out on the water — depends on models that are only as good as the data and tools behind them. As a Performance Intern within Hardware Engineering, you'll work on exactly that: the modeling backbone used to predict and validate Seaglider performance for both vehicle development and day-to-day operations. You'll build on a framework created by interns before you, strengthening the connection between real on-water test data and the models that predict how Seagliders perform, and pushing that work toward generating performance data in standardized, repeatable formats.

Job Description

An experimental postdoctoral research position is available in NLR’s Materials Discovery and Development group. The position is focused on thin film synthesis and characterization of nitride materials by physical vapor deposition (sputtering). The position would support several collaborative basic science and applied development projects exploring emerging nitride thin films for applications including semiconductors, ultrawide bandgap semiconductors, piezo/ferroelectric materials, and radiation detectors.

One of the projects that this position would support is NLR’s next-generation autonomous semiconductor development suite, created as part of the U.S. Department of Energy's METALLIC platform. Through METALLIC, NLR aims to accelerate the discovery of advanced thin film inorganic semiconductor materials to address critical U.S. supply chain challenges, with particular emphasis on semiconductor technologies involving Ga, Ge, Sc and other critical elements and materials. This position will focus on the development of sputter deposition processes and characterization workflows using this autonomous semiconductor suite. Other projects that would be supported by this position focus on the design, development, and testing of novel ultrawide bandgap nitride materials for radiation detection and piezoelectric/ferroelectric devices.

As a part of both projects, the successful candidate will design and perform thin film synthesis and characterization experiments, collaborate with other scientists and engineers at NLR and at partner institutions, and disseminate results in the form of conference presentations and scientific publications. The job duties would also include setting up and maintaining existing experimental equipment and improving/creating data collection and analysis tools.

Note: We encourage anyone who is interested in this opportunity to apply, even if they don't meet 100% of the position requirements. We seek dedicated people who believe they have the credentials, skills, and ambition to succeed at NLR to apply for this role.

- Established track record in scientific writing, presentation, publishing, and communication.
